title: External inflammatory resorption
topic: Damaged root surface + infected canal = external inflammatory resorption of root and bone; treating the canal early arrests it.

claims.claim: Damaged root surface (luxation, avulsion) + infected canal = inflammatory resorption
claims.source: Fuss Z, Tsesis I, Lin S. Dent Traumatol 2003;19:175-82 (PMID 12848710) - abstract

claims.claim: Toxins via dentinal tubules reach the denuded surface; intact cementum blocks them (schematic: a theory from monkey histology)
claims.source: Andreasen JO. J Endod 1981;7:294-301 (PMID 6942086); reprint J Endod 2021;47:865-72 (PMID 33975756) - abstract of reprint

claims.claim: Root + bone resorb: bowl-shaped craters in the root and the facing bone (schematic cutaway, not to scale)
claims.source: Abbott PV. Aust Dent J 2016;61 Suppl 1:82-94 (PMID 26923450); Lin S et al. Dent Traumatol 2022;38:253-66 (PMID 35559593)

claims.claim: By week 1: inflammatory resorption seen on histology (monkey)
claims.source: Andreasen JO. Swed Dent J 1980;4:101-10 (PMID 6933704) - abstract

claims.claim: ~1 month: usually visible on X-ray (replanted human incisors)
claims.source: Andreasen JO, Borum MK, Jacobsen HL, Andreasen FM. Endod Dent Traumatol 1995;11:76-89 (PMID 7641622) - abstract

claims.claim: Months: untreated, the root can be lost (review-level statement; timeline schematic)
claims.source: Patel S, Saberi N, Pimental T, Teng PH. Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - review full text

claims.claim: "Very rapid in children" (quoted consensus wording, not a measured rate)
claims.source: Fouad AF et al. (IADT). Dent Traumatol 2020;36:331-42 (PMID 32460393), sect. 10 - guideline full text

claims.claim: Disinfect the canal + Ca(OH)2 dressing: stimulus cut, resorption arrests; crater is lined, not refilled (schematic)
claims.source: Fuss Z et al. Dent Traumatol 2003;19:175-82 (PMID 12848710); Bourguignon C et al. (IADT). Dent Traumatol 2020;36:314-30 (PMID 32475015), sect. 13.3

claims.claim: 97% healed: 192 of 197 teeth with inflammatory resorption (luxated non-vital incisors, Ca(OH)2 then GP, radiographic, retrospective); 5 went on to ankylosis
claims.source: Cvek M. Endod Dent Traumatol 1992;8:45-55 (PMID 1521505) - abstract

claims.claim: Replanted mature (closed-apex) tooth: start RCT within 2 weeks
claims.source: Fouad AF et al. (IADT). Dent Traumatol 2020;36:331-42 (PMID 32460393), sect. 10 - guideline full text

caption:
External inflammatory resorption = damaged root surface + infected canal.
After luxation/avulsion, toxins from an infected pulp reach the denuded root via tubules (theory); root and bone resorb. By week 1 on monkey histology, usually on X-ray by ~1 month. Canal treated: 192 of 197 teeth with inflammatory resorption healed (luxated non-vital incisors, Ca(OH)2 then GP, retrospective). IADT 2020: replanted closed-apex tooth, start RCT within 2 weeks.
Schematic animation.
Refs: Fuss 2003 Dent Traumatol; Andreasen 1981 J Endod; Andreasen 1980 Swed Dent J; Andreasen 1995, Cvek 1992 Endod Dent Traumatol; Fouad 2020 Dent Traumatol
